svg.title: What each call read
svg.desc: Nineteen bars, one per model call of the first server run, grouped by step. The deriver read 923 tokens for session 1 and 1,115 for session 2. Dream 1: the deduction agent's four rounds read 2,460 to 3,069 tokens, the induction agent's three 1,028 to 1,705. Dream 2: the deduction agent's five rounds read 2,551 to 4,069, the induction agent's four 1,028 to 2,861. In every round of an agent, the part equal to its first round is sent again; the rest is what it has read since. The dialectic's one call read 4,598 tokens. In all, 49,585 tokens, 44,987 of them for writing.
svg.text: The 19 model calls of the first server run. The dream agents make most of them, and each round sends the agent's
sent again every round (as in round 1)
Writing the two sessions took 18 calls and 44,987 tokens; the dialectic's call that gave the answer its context, 4,598 more. The second dream cost
more than the first because its tool results were longer: both asked for the newest twenty conclusions.
From the first run of a Honcho 3.3.0 server on the example; tokens as reported by the model's provider
